name: PTSD
description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder can develop after experiencing or witnessing a traumatic event, causing intrusive memories, avoidance, hyperarousal, and negative changes in thinking and mood.

immediateActions.title: Trauma-Informed Grounding: Hold & Name
instructions: Find a safe, seated position with both feet flat on the floor
Pick up a small object near you (pen, stone, keys, fabric)
Hold it in both hands and notice every detail: texture, temperature, weight, edges
Say 3 things you notice about it out loud or in your head
Name the room you are in and 3 objects you can see
Tell yourself silently: I am here. I am safe now. This moment is not then.
Take 4 slow breaths: in for 5, out for 7

immediateActions.title: Window of Tolerance Reset
instructions: Notice whether you feel hypo-aroused (numb, frozen) or hyper-aroused (panicked, agitated)
For hyper-arousal: place one hand on chest, one on belly, breathe only into the belly hand for 10 breaths
For hypo-arousal: stand up, stamp feet gently 10 times, rub arms firmly, splash cold water on face
After either sequence, say your name, today's date, and your location out loud
Find one thing in the room that gives you even a tiny sense of safety and focus on it for 30 seconds

immediateActions.title: Container Exercise
instructions: Imagine a container — a box, safe, chest, vault — whatever feels right to you
Picture it in detail: material, locks, size, color
Take intrusive images, thoughts, or memories and mentally place them one by one inside the container
Close and lock the container securely
Imagine placing the container somewhere outside of you — another room, underground, wherever feels safest
Tell yourself: I can choose to open this when I am ready and with support. Right now, these are stored safely away.
Bring attention back to your breath and your body in the present

safetyGuidance: PTSD is a treatable condition and you are not broken; your nervous system learned to protect you and now needs help feeling safe again. Evidence-based therapies like EMDR, CBT, and somatic therapies can be deeply effective. If you are experiencing PTSD symptoms, please consider working with a trauma-specialised mental health professional. If you ever feel unsafe, contact your local crisis line or emergency services immediately. Recovery is possible and you deserve skilled support on your journey.
